description: A member leaves a partially completed project in shared storage, and staff must know what instructions, materials, hazards, and ownership notes are attached to it before anyone else moves or touches it. All projects and spaces are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 38-year-old floor supervisor managing a crowded shared project area
user_profile.context: Unlabeled or partially labeled projects are beginning to create safety and ownership confusion in the shared space
user_profile.communication_style: Boundary-conscious and practical, wants stored projects tied to clear status and handling notes

fact_sheet.fact: All projects in shared storage must have a 'MakerTrack' QR code tag, model TT-45, affixed to the primary container.
Project 'Astro-Gnomon' is assigned Project ID PJ-7781.
Project 'Synth-Shell' is assigned Project ID PJ-8102.
Alina Vance, member ID M-1138, is the owner of project PJ-7781.
Kenji Tanaka, member ID M-2049, is the owner of project PJ-8102.
Alina Vance's contact email is alina.vance@email.fake and her emergency contact number is 555-0101.
Project PJ-7781 is currently located in Shared Storage Bay C-04 on the second shelf.
Project PJ-8102 is located in the Electronics Work-in-Progress cabinet, locker E-12.
Projects left without a valid, scannable QR tag for more than 24 hours are moved to the 'Quarantine Shelf' in Zone D.
A project is considered 'inactive' if its QR tag has not been scanned by the owner for 7 consecutive days.
Inactive projects are red-tagged by floor staff and a notification is sent via the MakerTrack system.
Red-tagged projects are disposed of after 14 days if the owner does not update the project status.
Project PJ-7781, 'Astro-Gnomon', is a kinetic sculpture made of aluminum and brass components.
The current status of PJ-7781 is 'Awaiting custom gear fabrication'; last updated on October 26, 2023.
Project PJ-8102, 'Synth-Shell', is a custom-molded case for a modular synthesizer.
The next step for PJ-8102 is 'sanding and priming the resin cast'.
To continue work on PJ-7781, the owner needs access to the Tormach 1100M CNC mill.
Project PJ-8102 requires 220-grit sandpaper and aerosol-based plastic primer, which is stored in the Flammables Cabinet #2.
Project PJ-7781 has a handling note: 'Caution: contains unfinished, sharp aluminum edges. Wear cut-resistant Level 3 gloves when moving'.
Project PJ-8102 involves 'Epoxy Resin X-45', which requires nitrile gloves and mandatory use of Ventilation Hood #3 during mixing.
The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for 'Epoxy Resin X-45' is located in a binder labeled 'Resins and Adhesives' next to the chemical storage.
Maya Corrigan is the Floor Supervisor responsible for Zones A, B, and C.
Leo Martinez is the designated Safety Officer; his extension is 445.
When an untagged project is found, staff must fill out 'Incident Form 11-B' and upload a photo to the '#storage-audits' Slack channel.
The floor supervisor must perform a full audit of storage bays C and D every Friday at 4:00 PM.
Any spills or evidence of chemical leaks must be immediately reported to Leo Martinez before cleanup is attempted.
The MakerTrack project management system is accessible at the URL: https://makerspace.internal/makertrack.
Staff log into MakerTrack using their 'SparkWorks ID' credentials.
The 'MakerTrack Mobile' app for staff is available on the internal network for Android devices, version 2.1.4.
Automated email notifications for red-tagged projects are sent from the address 'noreply@makertrack.sparkworks.dev'.
The makerspace is named 'SparkWorks Community Forge'.
The shared project storage area is located in the northwest corner of the main workshop floor.
The first aid station nearest to the shared storage is located next to the main exit, Station B.
A notice about the 14-day disposal policy for red-tagged items was sent to all members via the monthly newsletter on October 1, 2023.
A physical copy of the complete storage policy, document #POL-STOR-003, is posted on the bulletin board at the entrance to the storage area.
